title: Finite base field torsion cohomological dimension bound
statement: Let $K$ be a finite field. Every torsion abelian sheaf on the small étale site of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ has vanishing ordinary derived global-section cohomology in every degree greater than one. Equivalently, the torsion étale cohomological dimension of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ is at most one.

source.place: finite-field torsion bound, paragraphs Reduction to finite modules through Consequences

proof.text: Use the geometric-stalk equivalence with discrete absolute Galois modules and the section/invariants comparison. For finite $K$, the absolute Galois group is the profinite completion of the integers.

Every torsion discrete module for the profinite integers is the directed union of finite stable submodules. Continuous cohomology commutes with this directed union and with the colimit over finite cyclic quotients.

For a finite stable module, choose an exponent annihilating it and factor the action through a finite cyclic quotient. Inflation along the quotient map from a cyclic group of order $n$ to one of order $en$ is zero in every degree at least two when the module is killed by $e$. Hence the cyclic quotient colimit vanishes in those degrees.
Transfer the vanishing from continuous Galois cohomology to étale cohomology of every torsion sheaf, then unfold HasTorsionEtaleCohomologicalDimensionLE.
